action.name: Queued: the place in line is the run's output

description: Fires once per PR head and base pair when the conflict watch (d31) finds the PR CONFLICTING with its base branch: GitHub sends no webhook for it, so the node reads the open PRs of vars.fixer_repos every vars.conflict_watch_interval_s (default 600 s). Same-repo, non-draft, open PRs of repos in vars.fixer_repos only; vars.fixer_excluded_repos overrides it. Adds the PR to the fixer queue (#35, d29: workflow queue-add) like pr-fixer-checks; the agent merges the base branch's tip at dispatch (d37: the merge paragraph names it) and resolves the conflict, and the gate allows that one merge from base and judges only its resolution. Shares the per-PR concurrency key with the other pr-fixer-* rules but is not an attempt itself. Only while the PR is open.
name: PR fixer: conflict with base

on_failure.name: Hand back with the run link (once per chain)

params.body: PR fixer handed back ({{ run.error.code }}): {{ run.error.message }}

inputs.instruction: PR {{ trigger.data.repository }}#{{ trigger.data.number }} conflicts with its base branch {{ trigger.data.base_branch }} at {{ trigger.data.head_sha }}. Work on the PR head branch {{ trigger.data.head_branch }} only. Merge the base branch into it as exactly one real two-parent merge of the base commit named in the merge paragraph below (the base branch's tip when this try was dispatched; one merge, never a rebase, never another commit) and resolve every conflict, keeping the intent of both sides; where both sides bump a version or add a changelog entry, keep the base's and put the PR's above it with the next version. Make no other change. Never edit .github/workflows, never delete or skip tests and never add suppression markers.
